headline: Saima Wazed resigns as WHO regional head following fraud and forgery allegations
summary: Saima Wazed Putul, daughter of ousted PM Sheikh Hasina, stepped down from her WHO Southeast Asia role amid investigations by the UN agency and Bangladeshi authorities into alleged financial fraud and misrepresentation of credentials.
details: Saima Wazed Putul, the World Health Organization's Southeast Asia head and daughter of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, resigned on Wednesday. Her resignation follows fraud investigations by the UN agency and Bangladeshi authorities.

The case highlights how the fallout from Hasina's ouster around mid-2024 has extended to her family members, beyond her political allies. Many of Hasina's associates now face criminal charges or live in self-imposed exile.

The WHO placed Putul on unpaid administrative leave late last year, after she took office in early 2024 for a five-year term. Bangladesh's Anti-Corruption Commission had filed charges against her in March, alleging fraud and forgery.

The WHO accused Putul of "committing financial fraud in relation to her travel to China" involving $901, and of misrepresenting her academic credentials. Putul, through her lawyers, has denied these allegations, stating the travel issue was an administrative oversight and her doctorate is honorary for autism work.

Additionally, the WHO alleged she illegally acquired a plot of land in Bangladesh. Putul stated she acquired the land before joining the WHO and was entitled to it under a Bangladeshi law covering families of the country's independence leader, Sheikh Mujibur Rahman.

In her resignation letter to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Putul expressed a loss of trust due to being prevented from carrying out her duties. She also cited an untenable financial situation after nearly a year without remuneration.

The WHO had previously stated Putul was on leave but declined further comment to maintain confidentiality. Sources indicated the UN agency was planning to formally remove her, with nominations for the role expected on October 12.

Regional directors are influential health policy officials, responsible for outbreak responses and adapting WHO policies. They are elected every five years by member states in their respective regions.

headline_marked: Actor Arsh Khan: [[We've forgotten humanity]] amidst political divisions, 'July fighter' term corrupted
headline: Actor Arsh Khan: We've forgotten humanity amidst political divisions, 'July fighter' term corrupted
summary: Actor Arsh Khan expressed his reluctance to be called a 'July fighter,' stating the term has lost its value and integrity. He also condemned recent mobbing incidents, including the harassment of actress Azmeri Haque Badhon.
details: Actor Arsh Khan, who actively participated in the July 2024 mass uprising both on the streets and social media, recently shared his views on the movement and current societal issues. He spoke from a shooting location in Uttara, Dhaka, during a drama production.

Khan expressed discomfort with being identified as a 'July fighter,' stating that the term has lost its inherent value, honesty, and neutrality. He believes the phrase has become 'ugly' due to exploitation by many for personal gain.

Despite his reservations about the term, Arsh Khan affirmed he has no regrets about joining the July movement. He emphasized that he took to the streets for the students, particularly those from schools in Uttara, who are not involved in politics but are focused on their studies.

He declared his readiness to protest again for the students if necessary, stating he would go to any lengths for them. Khan also highlighted a significant difference in understanding with those who participated in the movement for political power rather than genuine cause.

Addressing the recent harassment of actress Azmeri Haque Badhon, Khan condemned all forms of mob violence. He stressed that legal channels should be pursued if there are suspicions or complexities regarding anyone, especially since the country is now calm.

Khan noted that for years, people have witnessed women being beaten on the streets, implying this is not a new phenomenon. He believes that society has forgotten that 'humanity is above all,' prioritizing political affiliations like Awami League, BNP, and Jamaat over shared human identity.

He firmly stated his opposition to any form of harassment, whether against women, men, or artists. Khan advocated for dialogue or legal action against those with whom one disagrees or believes have committed wrong, rather than resorting to mob justice.
